The most common and infamous of the cave worms gives its name to the entire family—a much-feared monster wandering the twisting tunnels of the Darklands that is capable of carving out entire cave systems. Tunnels bored by a cave worm don't always last long after these creature's passage, and areas where they nest are maddening mazes of passageways that lead nowhere, yet navigating the labyrinth to find the worm's central nest often yields amazing treasures left behind by the worm's prior victims. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Cave Worm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2871) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 54 1.1 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 100 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +30 **Str** +9 **Dex** -1 **Con** +7 **Int** -5 **Wis** -1 **Cha** -1 --- **AC** 32 **Fort** +28 **Ref** +21 **Will** +21 **HP** 270 **Inexorable** The cave worm recovers from the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) condition, and it ignores [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) and greater difficult terrain.
**Slough Skin** **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** The cave worm would be affected by a condition or adverse effect (such as [_cursed metamorphosis_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479)); **Effect** The cave worm negates the triggering condition or effect by sloughing an outer layer of its skin. Effects from [artifacts](/Traits.aspx?ID=537), deities, or a similarly powerful source can't be avoided in this way. --- **Speed** 40 feet, burrow 40 feet, swim 20 feet **Melee** jaws +28 ([deadly 2d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+15 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Melee** stinger +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+15 piercing plus cave worm venom **Melee** body +26 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d10+13 bludgeoning **Ranged** regurgitate +26 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** varies (see ability) **Cave Worm Venom** ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 32 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 5d6 poison damage and [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) (1 round); **Stage 2** 6d6 poison damage, and enfeebled 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 8d6 poison damage and enfeebled 2 (1 round) **Fast Swallow** **Trigger** The cave worm [Grabs](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) a creature; **Effect** The worm uses Swallow Whole. **Regurgitate** The cave worm can violently regurgitate a creature or boulder it has swallowed to make a ranged Strike. The Strike deals bludgeoning damage depending on the size of the projectile: Tiny deals 2d6+13, Small 3d6+13, Medium 4d6+13, Large 5d6+13, and Huge 6d6+13. A regurgitated creature takes [falling damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) from the height of the target or from 20 feet, whichever is greater. Boulders occupy space in the worm's stomach as a creature of equivalent size, and cave worms often have several boulders swallowed. A cave worm can use a single action to swallow a new boulder. **Rock Tunneler** A cave worm can burrow through solid stone at a Speed of 20 feet. It can leave a tunnel if it desires, and it usually does. **[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15)) Huge, 3d6+9 bludgeoning, Rupture 24 **Thrash** The worm attempts one Strike against each creature in its reach. It can Strike up to once with its jaws, up to once with its stinger, and any number of times with its body. Each attack counts toward the worm's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all the attacks.

An outcrop of dense stone that spends ages eroding can gain sapience and slowly awaken with the wisdom of nature. Such elemental beings are slow to action and difficult to anger, spurred only by immediate threats. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Elder Outcrop](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2626) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 105 2.0 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) 120 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +29, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +25, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +26, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +26 **Str** +8 **Dex** -2 **Con** +8 **Int** +1 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +29 **Ref** +19 **Will** +26 **HP** 295 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Dust Eternal** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55)) 30 feet. Dust swirls about the outcrop, rendering everything within its aura (including the outcrop) [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4). In addition, the dust at the outcrop's base creates [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) on the ground within the aura. The outcrop can activate or deactivate this aura using a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.
**Unstoppable** The elder outcrop's [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) condition can't exceed slowed 1, and it ignores penalties to its Speeds and the [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) condition. --- **Speed** 30 feet, burrow 30 feet; earth glide **Melee** column +27 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+14 bludgeoning plus [Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=20) **Ranged** rock +27 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d6+14 bludgeoning plus call of earth **Call of Earth** ([Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) A flying creature hit by the elder outcrop's rock ranged strike is affected by a 7th-rank [_earthbind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=94) spell (DC 33). **Earth Glide** The elder outcrop can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93) through any earthen matter, including rock. When it does so, the elder outcrop moves at its full burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of its passing. **Natural Formation** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) Until the next time it acts, the elder outcrop appears to be a natural terrain feature. It has an automatic result of 47 on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks and DCs to pass as a natural outcropping of rock. The outcrop's dust eternal aura is deactivated while Natural Formation is being used. **Stone Grip** ([Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) Great fingers of stone arise to grasp up to two Medium or smaller creatures on the ground in the outcrop's aura. Each target must succeed at a DC 33 Reflex save or be [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) by the stone hand (or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) on a critical failure; [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 33). A creature grabbed or restrained by a stone hand at the end of its turn becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) or increases its existing slowed condition by 1. When a creature is unable to act due to the slowed condition from this effect, the creature is permanently [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=30). **[Throw Rock](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=38)**

<title level="1" pfs="">[Elven Court Guard](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3634)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

In the tangled web of lineages, rivalries, and shifting alliances that is an elven noble court, aristocratic families employ bodyguards loyal to them alone.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 31

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 13">[Elven Court Guard](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3634)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=588" />
<trait label="Humanoid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=628" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [NPC Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=236) pg. 180

**Perception** +24; plus vigilance

**Languages**
[Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); plus one regional language

**Skills**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +26, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +23, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +24, [Heraldry Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +21, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +19

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +4

**Dex** +5

**Con** +2

**Int** +2

**Wis** +3

**Cha** +1
</row>

**Vigilance** A court guard gains a +1 circumstance bonus on Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) and [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) creatures, and if they succeed, they get a critical success instead.

**Items**
_+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) [chain shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=43)_, _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [low-grade cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) [elven curve blade](/Weapons.aspx?ID=406)_, _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [composite longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=434)_

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 35 

**Fort** +20 

**Ref** +27 

**Will** +23 

+1 status vs. [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 225

</row>

**Interposition** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An ally within 15 feet of the guard would take damage; **Effect** The guard Strides. This movement does not trigger reactions, and the guard must end the Stride in a space adjacent to the ally. The guard then switches places with the ally, taking all damage and associated effects instead of the ally.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 30 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_elven curve blade_ +27 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)),
**Damage** 2d8+12 slashing

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
fist +26 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188), [Unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199)),
**Damage** 1d4+12 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
_composite longbow_ +27 ([deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [volley 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=201)),
**Damage** 2d8+10 piercing

**Avenge the Fallen** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76)) **Frequency** once per round; **Requirements** The guard is within 30 feet of the creature they were guarding, and that creature is either [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) or died since the guard's last turn; **Effect** The guard Strikes the creature that damaged their ally. They roll the attack roll twice and use the higher result.

**Dancing Blade** <actions string="Two Actions" />  The guard makes a Strike against a creature, then Strides. This Stride doesn't trigger reactions. If the guard ends this Stride in a different space adjacent to the same creature, they make another Strike against it. If both Strikes succeed, the creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of the guard's next turn. Each attack counts toward the guard's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until they've made both attacks.

</column>

<title level="1" pfs="">[Globetrotting Scholar](/NPCs.aspx?ID=3595)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

It takes a particular kind of personality to leave the creature comforts of academia in order to explore trap-ridden ancient tombs or observe man-eating monstrosities in their native habitats. The sort of personality that finds joy in the life cycle of parasitic wasps or recounts grisly Ghol-Gani sacrificial rites with a decidedly gruesome relish. Academia would not survive without such globetrotting scholars, but to their more sedate colleagues, they do tend to come off as an odd bunch.

A greater chimera can have any combination of three heads chosen from the options below, each granting additional abilities inherent in the original creature. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Greater Chimera](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3257) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 133 2.1 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +22, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +27 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** -2 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +1 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +23 **Will** +20 **HP** 235 **Multiple Reactions** A greater chimera gains 2 extra reactions each round that it can use only to make Reactive Strikes. It must use a different head for each reaction, and it can't use more than one on the same triggering action. If it loses one of its heads, it also loses one of these extra reactions.
**Three-Headed** Any ability that would sever a greater chimera's head (such as a critical hit with a [_vorpal_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2853) weapon) severs one head at random. Losing a head doesn't kill a chimera (as long as it has at least one head left), but it does prevent it from making Strikes with the lost head or using any abilities granted by the head.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** claw +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)), **Damage** 3d8+8 slashing **Three-Headed Strike** The greater chimera makes a Strike with each of its heads, each at a –2 penalty and targeting a different creature. These Strikes count as only one attack for the greater chimera's multiple attack penalty, and the penalty doesn't increase until after it has made all three attacks.

Resembling twisted lumps of fused gravel with oddly angled crystal limbs, gritblights are shock troops commonly used by [Ayrzul](/Deities.aspx?ID=102) to spread terror and disease to his enemies. These creatures are the gruesome result of experiments on crystalline elementals who were once the allies or servants of Ayrzul's rival lord of elemental earth, [Sairazul](/Deities.aspx?ID=107). Their crystalline body parts appear cracked and deformed, only their single “eye” left intact. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Gritblight](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3732) **Source** [Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay](/Sources.aspx?ID=243) pg. 84 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), blight sense ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 60 feet, [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet, grit vision **Languages** [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +21, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** +0 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +1 **Blight Sense** A gritblight can detect the location of nearby creatures afflicted with [Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41) as a precise sense at the listed range.
**Grit Vision** A gritblight's vision is unaffected by clouds of sand, dirt, grit, or other earth materials in air or water. --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +19 **Will** +23 +1 status vs. [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585) effects **HP** 235 **Immunities** bleed, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 15, physical 15 **Blight Cloud** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [radiation](/Traits.aspx?ID=421)) 30 feet. A gritblight continually sheds tiny fragments of radioactive earth in a cloud around it. This cloud conceals the gritblight as a light fog and sheds [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) in the area. Any creature that begins its turn in the aura takes 2d6 poison damage with a DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. A creature that fails its save is exposed to [Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41) and a creature that critically fails is additionally [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91). --- **Speed** 30 feet, burrow 30 feet; earth glide **Melee** claw +27 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d6+14 slashing plus 2d6 acid **Ranged** caustic shard +23 ([range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d6+10 piercing plus 2d6 acid **[Ayrzul's Blight](/Diseases.aspx?ID=41)** ([Disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [Earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) but DC 33. **Earth Glide** The gritblight can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) through any earthen matter, including rock. When it does so, the gritblight moves at its full burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of its passing. **Labyrinthine Vision** ([Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The gritblight forces disorienting visions of Ayrzul's Blistering Labyrinth into the minds of nearby creatures. All creatures in a 60-foot cone take 7d12 mental damage with a DC 33 Will save. Creatures [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) by a gritblight's Labyrinthine Vision see only endless earthen tunnels in every direction. The gritblight can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is blinded for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is blinded permanently. **[Trample](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=81)** Medium or smaller, claw, DC 33

**Urban Legend** A brainchild is sustained only by the reputation that precedes them. Mindless creatures are immune to a brainchild and can't perceive them. The brainchild's size, features, and items, as well as the appearance of their attacks, match what the foes perceiving them expect. If foes expect to see different things, the brainchild chooses which to manifest. If any creature that can perceive the brainchild believes the brainchild has one of the abilities below, the brainchild has that ability. A creature can Seek or Sense Motive (against the brainchild's Deception DC) to attempt to disbelieve an individual ability. If at any point no creature perceiving the brainchild believes in the ability, the brainchild loses that ability immediately. If foes expect different particulars, such as one believing the brainchild is immune to fire and another believing they're immune to divinations, the brainchild chooses one to have. Abilities that can be disbelieved include his resistance to physical damage, his frightful presence, the slashing damage from his Strikes, and his 7th-level innate spells

The target can't be returned to life through any means, even powerful magic like wish, until the corrupted Willowshore mindscape is destroyed.

When a group of diabolists or worshippers of an archdevil come to an ignominious end, their souls can sometimes be caught between life and death, unable or unwilling to pass on to the afterlife due to the humiliation of their untimely deaths. When enough closely-associated worshippers whose souls aren't already claimed in existing contracts meet such a fate, the spiritual “weight” of this shame can cause them to merge into a conglomeration of infernally-infused spirits—a hellshadow. Hellshadows look like a bank of fire and smoke, yet the flames themselves are made of distorted bodies and faces. The hellshadow constantly exudes a cloud of smoke that scorches flesh but leaves other materials unharmed. Living creatures who start their turn in this aura take 2d6 fire damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex). On a critical failure, the creature is also [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91). --- **Speed** fly 40 feet **Melee** brimstone tendrils +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519)), **Damage** 3d8+6 fire plus 2d6 void and clinging smoke **Divine Innate Spells** DC 33, attack +25 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Divine Lance](/Spells.aspx?ID=84), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745) - **6th** [Crisis of Faith](/Spells.aspx?ID=55), [Divine Immolation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1496) - **7th** [Divine Decree](/Spells.aspx?ID=82), [Shadow Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=273) (fire or spirit only) **Clinging Smoke** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) A creature that takes damage from the hellshadow's brimstone tendrils Strike has coils of the creature's smoke solidify around their body, impeding movement. The creature must attempt a DC 33 Reflex save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The smoke solidifies as it coils around their limbs, imposing a –5-foot status penalty to all Speeds until the end of the creature's next turn.
**Failure** As success, except –10 feet to speed and the creature is also clumsy 1 until the end of their next turn.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the creature is also slowed 1 until the end of their next turn.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Iron Warden](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3068)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Traditionally crafted into the forms of giant suits of armor or powerful animals, iron wardens are products of exquisite artistry and skill. Their articulated joints and sturdy, armored bodies require great care and mathematical precision to craft, and regular cleaning and oiling ensure they don't rust over the ages. With proper care, iron wardens can remain in good shape for thousands of years, being passed down for generations, as long as they aren't destroyed by meddlesome adventurers. In addition to their incredible strength, iron wardens possess a potent toxic breath that is often more than enough to dispatch entire groups of opponents.

 Though their impressive stature prevents them from being inconspicuous, iron wardens are often placed in areas where they are easily mistaken for decorative objects. An iron warden might be hidden among decorative suits of armor or disguised as a statue in a city square. Occasionally, locals are shocked when something they assumed to be a historic landmark animates into an iron warden, called to action by an unknown mystic command. Stories tell of ancient civilizations, such as the Jistka Imperium, that created iron wardens of massive size. Most of these constructs have since been melted down for resources, but magicians and historians still chase down rumors of one of these lost colossi.

description:
Traditionally crafted into the forms of giant suits of armor or powerful animals, iron wardens are products of exquisite artistry and skill. Their articulated joints and sturdy, armored bodies require great care and mathematical precision to craft, and regular cleaning and oiling ensure they don't rust over the ages. With proper care, iron wardens can remain in good shape for thousands of years, being passed down for generations, as long as they aren't destroyed by meddlesome adventurers. In addition to their incredible strength, iron wardens possess a potent toxic breath that is often more than enough to dispatch entire groups of opponents.

 Though their impressive stature prevents them from being inconspicuous, iron wardens are often placed in areas where they are easily mistaken for decorative objects. An iron warden might be hidden among decorative suits of armor or disguised as a statue in a city square. Occasionally, locals are shocked when something they assumed to be a historic landmark animates into an iron warden, called to action by an unknown mystic command. Stories tell of ancient civilizations, such as the Jistka Imperium, that created iron wardens of massive size. Most of these constructs have since been melted down for resources, but magicians and historians still chase down rumors of one of these lost colossi.

The heavy suit of mechanical metal armor a juggernaut wears is custom-built and highly complex and specialized to its wearer. When two melomachs meet, the resulting contests of physical might and vocal prowess can last for days, often leaving the landscape ravaged for miles in every direction.

With its mottled green-and-tan rubbery flesh, six short legs ending in two-clawed feet, and three circular mouths arrayed equidistantly around a disk-shaped head crowned by multiple bulbous eyes, the bizarre Darklands-dwelling ockomlire's strange appearance blurs the line between aberration and fungus. Ockomlires eat magic, and their specialized organs process and release that magic in the form of a mist that saps the willpower of those it touches. Originally created by [sekmin](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=468) occultists as a potent weapon against Azlanti wizards, since the serpentfolk empire's collapse thousands of years ago, ockomlires have spread upward through the Darklands. They often lair in sewers or abandoned basements in urban areas, drawn to society's use (and waste) of magical energy. Ockomlires are quite intelligent but tend to have bland personalities. They're fond of verbalizing their observations and experiences, speaking in unsettling piping voices through three mouths; they have a curious penchant for referring to themselves in the third person. They've little interest in having personal names and tend to refer to those they encounter by ancestry instead of name as well. **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Ockomlire](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3741) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 87 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +24, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +23 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +0 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +21 **Will** +23 +1 status to all saves vs [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effects **HP** 235 **Resistances** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 15 **Weaknesses** emotion vulnerability **Emotion Vulnerability** If an ockomlire fails a saving throw against an emotion effect, they loses their resistance to mental damage and gains an equal amount of weakness to mental damage (weakness to mental 15 for the typical ockomlire) until the end of their next turn. --- **Speed** 20 feet, climb 10 feet **Melee** jaws +27 ([Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=180)), **Damage** 3d10+14 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **7th** [Calm](/Spells.aspx?ID=1458) (at will) - **Constant (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) **Devour Magic** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The ockomlire attempts to devour a spell effect from a creature they've [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77). To successfully do so, they must [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) that effect with an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check. If the spell effect is an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effect, the ockomlire gains a +2 circumstance bonus to this check.
**Critical Success** The spell is countered, the ockomlire gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the spell's rank for 1 minute, and the grabbed creature becomes [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 minute.
**Success** As success but stupefied 1.
**Critical Failure** The attempt backfires, and the ockomlire becomes overwhelmed; their emotion vulnerability becomes active until the end of their turn. **Haze of Despair** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirements** The ockomlire has temporary hit points gained from Devour Magic; **Effects** The ockomlire digests the magic and releases mist that stings the eyes and heart alike. The ockomlire loses any temporary Hit Points they have and all non-ockomlire creatures in a 30-foot emanation take 9d10 mental damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save).
name: Ockomlire

The shifting shapes of clouds in the sky have captivated the imaginations of mortal children for centuries. Pictures-in-clouds represent this pure possibility of air, transforming into anything the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) imagines them to be. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Picture-in-Cloud](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2619) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 83 2.0 **Perception** +20; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +24 **Str** +4 **Dex** +8 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 35 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +26 **Will** +19 **HP** 175 **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **High Winds** ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206)) 60 feet. Air within the emanation is difficult terrain for [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) creatures that don't have the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5) trait.
**Disperse** **Trigger** The picture-in-clouds takes damage from a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300); **Effect** The picture-inclouds disperses. Until the end of the current turn, they can't be attacked or targeted, they don't take up space, and any auras or emanations they have are suppressed. At the end of the turn, the picture-in-clouds re-forms in any sufficient space within 150 feet of where they dispersed; any auras or emanations they have are restored as long as the duration didn't run out while the elemental was dispersed. --- **Speed** fly 100 feet; swiftness **Melee** gust +26 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+10 bludgeoning plus [Push](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=25) 15 feet **Ranged** lightning lash +26 ([range increment 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d12 electricity **Cloudgaze** The picture-in-clouds shifts into their choice of an eagle shape, elephant shape, or sword shape. **Elephant Blast** **Requirements** The picture-in-clouds is in elephant shape; **Effect** The picture-in-clouds breathes out a 30-foot cone of air from their cloudy trunk. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 30 Fortitude save to stand their ground. A creature [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) into a solid object stops moving and takes 4d10 bludgeoning damage.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is pushed 20 feet.
**Failure** The creature is pushed 40 feet.
**Critical Failure** The creature is pushed 40 feet and knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). **Feather Storm** ([Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114)) **Requirements** The picture-in-clouds is in eagle shape; **Effect** The picture-in-clouds [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) 125 feet, flapping their wings and creating a barrier along their path. This barrier has the effects of [_wall of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=367) (DC 30) and lasts until the end of the picture-in-clouds's next turn. **Slicing Wind** **Requirements** The picture-in-clouds is in sword shape; **Effect** The picture-in-clouds spins, forming a whirlwind that deals 5d8 slashing damage in a 15-foot emanation (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). **Swiftness** The picture-in-clouds's movement doesn't trigger reactions.
name: Picture-in-Cloud

This big-headed beast is covered in glittering scales; its eyes are like large copper pots, and its mouth is full of sharp teeth. Despite its fish-like appearance, a quai dau to spends most of its time on land hunting along riversides or lakes. It uses its trunk to drain the nearby water before using it with deadly skill. A quai dau to can expel the water with a force strong enough to knock a knight off a horse, or gently enough to surround themself in a veil of mist. A quai dau to is extremely sensitive to sound. If they hear too much ruckus near their hunting grounds, they violently attack. Their silent movement allows them to sneak up on such distracted prey despite their massive size. Researchers have discovered, after much study, that quai dau tos don't have ears in the traditional sense. They have an organ in the upper part of their skulls that inflates to hold the water they use in their attacks. This organ is extremely sensitive to vibrations in the air and is used as a pseudo ear. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Quai Dau To](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3158) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 284 1.1 **Perception** +25; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), mist vision, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +25, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +8 **Int** -3 **Wis** +5 **Cha** -1 **Mist Vision** The quai dau to ignores the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) condition from mist and fog. --- **AC** 32 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +19 **Will** +21 **HP** 300 **Immunities** [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59), [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) **Weaknesses** [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 15 **Frightful Sight** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) 60 feet. This aura functions as a DC 32 [frightful presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64) aura, but a creature doesn't attempt its save until it sees the quai dau to.
**Reflective Scales** **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet casts a spell with the [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640) trait or uses an ability with the light trait; **Effect** The quai dau to adjusts its position to reflect the light off their scales in a blinding display. description:
This big-headed beast is covered in glittering scales; its eyes are like large copper pots, and its mouth is full of sharp teeth. Despite its fish-like appearance, a quai dau to spends most of its time on land hunting along riversides or lakes. It uses its trunk to drain the nearby water before using it with deadly skill. A quai dau to can expel the water with a force strong enough to knock a knight off a horse, or gently enough to surround themself in a veil of mist.

 A quai dau to is extremely sensitive to sound. If they hear too much ruckus near their hunting grounds, they violently attack. Their silent movement allows them to sneak up on such distracted prey despite their massive size. Researchers have discovered, after much study, that quai dau tos don't have ears in the traditional sense. They have an organ in the upper part of their skulls that inflates to hold the water they use in their attacks. This organ is extremely sensitive to vibrations in the air and is used as a pseudo ear.

The royal basilisk is aptly named, not for only the metal crown upon its head but also for the unique potency of its poison. The creature's poison manifests as a sort of cloying vapor that sticks onto and eats away at anything it touches. Their mastery of poison does appear to come at a cost, as the royal basilisk has no ability to petrify its prey. Although the royal basilisk can painstakingly shape a crown, some made of simple iron and others of rare skymetals, they much prefer to collect crowns crafted by other creatures. **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Royal Basilisk](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3255) **Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 127 2.1 **Perception** +27; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 120 feet, [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 60 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +24, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +25 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +7 **Int** -3 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +2 **Items** iron crown --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +22 **Will** +23 **HP** 290 **Immunities** [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 15 **Crowned Royalty** The royal basilisk's crown is firmly attached to its head but can be [Disarmed](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383) as though it were a held item. Without a crown, the royal basilisk's mastery over poison is weakened enough that it loses its miasmatic shroud. The royal basilisk can equip a crown within its tail's reach as an Interact action. A royal basilisk's crown is normally made of iron and enables the basilisk to use miasmatic shroud, but crowns made of other, more exotic materials might confer different abilities.
**Miasmatic Shroud** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) 15 feet. The poison in the breath of the royal basilisk makes the air around it a haze, [concealing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) it from all creatures outside the aura, but it cannot use this concealment to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405). When a creature ends its turn within the aura, it is exposed to royal basilisk venom. --- **Speed** 30 feet, climb 30 feet, swim 30 feet **Melee** jaws +27 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d10+11 piercing plus Improved Grab and royal basilisk venom **Melee** tail +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d8+11 bludgeoning **Ranged** spit +24 ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [range 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 5d10 poison plus royal basilisk venom **[Greater Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=65)** 4d8+3 bludgeoning, DC 32 **Royal Basilisk Venom** ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 36; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 2d10 poison and [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) (1 round); **Stage 2** 3d10 poison and clumsy 3 (1 round); **Stage 3** 4d10 poison, clumsy 3, and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (1 round) **Stone-Hewing Spit** ([Acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3)) The royal basilisk spits its poison with immense force, dealing 5d10 acid and 5d8 piercing damage (DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) to creatures in a 240-foot line and exposing each creature that took damage to royal basilisk venom. The line penetrates barriers with Hardness of less than 20, ignoring any bonuses they'd provide from cover. The royal basilisk can't use Stone-Hewing Spit again for 1d4 rounds. **[Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77)** Large, 5d10 acid damage, Rupture 30 **Wrap in Coils** **Requirements** A Large or smaller creature is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) in the royal basilisk's jaws; **Effect** The royal basilisk moves the creature into its coils, freeing its jaws to make attacks, then uses [Greater Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=65) against the creature. The royal basilisk's coils can hold as many creatures as will fit in its space.

The briny depths of the Boundless Sea sometimes twist large groups of merfolk into swarms with vicious rows of teeth and sharp claws known as saltborn stalkers. Saltborn stalkers hunt in groups, using their drooping, tentacle-like appendages as bioluminescent lures, posing them as wisps or bubbles of planar energy to draw unsuspecting prey into clever ambushes. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Saltborn Stalkers](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2666) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 186 2.0 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +22, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +22, [Plane of Water Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +22, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +26, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +22 **Str** +6 **Dex** +7 **Con** +5 **Int** +3 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +3 --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +22 **Ref** +26 **Will** +20 **HP** 240 (16 squares) **Immunities** bleed, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** area damage 10, [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage 10 **Saline Crust** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) 20 feet; **Requirements** The saltborn stalkers are in a body of water; **Effect** Layers of the saltborn's salty skin flake off to foul the water around them. A creature that ends its turn in the aura takes 2d6 acid damage with a DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save; creatures with the [amphibious](/Traits.aspx?ID=207) or [aquatic](/Traits.aspx?ID=168) trait are immune.
**[Troop Defenses](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=44)** --- **Speed** 10 feet, swim 60 feet; [troop movement](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=85) **Lightlure** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Effect** The saltborn stalkers move their luminescent lures in an entrancing light show, drawing nearby creatures into their grasp. Each creature in a 100-foot emanation must attempt a DC 33 Will save; regardless of the result of its save, the creature is then temporarily immune to Lightlure for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The creature is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) with the lures and must spend all its actions on its next turn to move closer to them as expediently as possible, avoiding obvious dangers along its path.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature is also [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1d4 rounds. **Salty Clutch** **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The stalkers reach out to Grab their foes and drag them underwater. Each enemy in a 5-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 33 Reflex save or be [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) by the stalkers (or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) on a critical success). For the rest of the current turn, the saltborn stalkers can move toward water or in water without ending the grab, carrying any grabbed or restrained creatures along with them. **Scour the Bones** **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The saltborn stalkers use their teeth and claws to vivisect each enemy in a 5-foot emanation (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The damage depends on the number of actions.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Shadow Giant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3016)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Shadow giants are natives of [the Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36), where they have dwelled in perpetual twilight for millennia. They live in familiar groups and uphold a nomadic way of life as they roam across ancestral lands between shadowy forests and misty chasms. These hunter-gatherers pass down lore through oral histories, conduct pilgrimages to unholy ziggurats of black stone, and bathe in the blood of their long-standing foes, including rival shadow giant clans and fiends of the Netherworld intent on enslaving their kind.

 Standing 15 feet tall, with gray skin and hair only a shade lighter, shadow giants are fearsome foes with a well-earned reputation as zealous warmongers and ruthless combatants. They rarely interact with outsiders, though they may treat with proven warriors who show the giants the respect and deference they feel they deserve.

description:
Shadow giants are natives of [the Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36), where they have dwelled in perpetual twilight for millennia. They live in familiar groups and uphold a nomadic way of life as they roam across ancestral lands between shadowy forests and misty chasms. These hunter-gatherers pass down lore through oral histories, conduct pilgrimages to unholy ziggurats of black stone, and bathe in the blood of their long-standing foes, including rival shadow giant clans and fiends of the Netherworld intent on enslaving their kind.

 Standing 15 feet tall, with gray skin and hair only a shade lighter, shadow giants are fearsome foes with a well-earned reputation as zealous warmongers and ruthless combatants. They rarely interact with outsiders, though they may treat with proven warriors who show the giants the respect and deference they feel they deserve.

Snow oni maintain their seething temperaments even in their icy homes. The isolation of their environment gives them trappings of asceticism, and many snow oni pursue physical perfection, reveling in the process of turning their bodies into powerful fighting machines. They are just as hedonistic and brutal as any of their brethren, however, and eager to indulge in warm baths, strong drink, and humanoid flesh. Like many oni, snow oni possess a third eye in the center of their forehead. This eye gives snow oni a mystical sense that allows them to peer through even the thickest flurries of snow. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Snow Oni](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3122) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 253 1.1 **Perception** +26; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), snow vision **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +25, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +27 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +5 **Int** +0 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +8 **Snow Vision** Snow doesn't impair the snow oni's vision; they ignore [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from snowfall. --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +25 **Will** +21 **HP** 290 **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) **Weaknesses** bean panic, spirit 15 **Bean Panic** Oni are curiously afraid of beans, especially as the seasons begin to change. If a creature Interacts to throw a handful of beans at the oni, the oni becomes [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). While frightened this way, their weakness to spirit damage is increased by 5. The oni then becomes immune to bean panic for 24 hours.
**Icy Deflection** **Trigger** The snow oni is targeted by a ranged Strike or spell attack roll that doesn't have the [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) trait; **Effect** The snow oni creates a reflective blockade of ice, gaining a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack roll. If the attack misses, the snow oni redirects the attack to another creature within 20 feet of the snow oni. The attacker rerolls the attack roll against the new target.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 40 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** fist +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d8+16 bludgeoning plus 2d6 cold **Melee** jaws +27 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d6+16 piercing plus 1d6 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Ranged** ice dart +25 ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d10+4 cold plus 1d6 spirit **Primal Innate Spells** DC 31 - **2nd** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (at will; self only) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=55)** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The snow oni can take on the appearance of any Medium or Large [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) creature. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage bonuses with their Strikes but might change the damage type their Strikes deal **Chilling Combo** ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27)) The snow oni makes two fist Strikes targeting the same creature. If they both hit, the target becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round. **Falling Frozen Lightning** ([Cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) The snow oni calls down a bolt of icy lightning, white as fallen snow. The bolt strikes a location within 60 feet, freezing the air into a cloud of snow that fills a 20-foot burst and lasts for 1 minute. All creatures within the snow become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and all creatures outside the snow become concealed to creatures within it. A creature that enters the snow or begins its turn there takes 15 cold damage, with a DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save.

The guillotine stands as the epitome of capital punishment in Galt. Yet despite its heinous reputation, most citizens consider it a clean and efficient means of political execution—at least, compared to the other options. One such alternative is the practice of drawing and quartering, a method where each of the victim's four limbs is tied to a different [horse](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=431). The horses are then spurred to run in opposite directions, with agonizing and gruesome results for the condemned. The locus of pain and resentment from such a death has been known to reanimate into an unusual conglomerate monster. Never again quite whole, a torn quartet is simplistic in its desire to mete out violence, usually starting with those responsible for its death. A torn quartet appears as four floating pieces of a humanoid cadaver, tethered together with ropes of spectral energy that each sport a single limb. One section might include a head, but it's largely nonfunctional. When one section is separated from its fellows, it drops to the ground and thrashes until reunited. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 33 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 [Torn Quartet](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3819) **Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 185 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20); (can't speak any language) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +27, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27 **Str** +5 **Dex** +8 **Con** +2 **Int** -2 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +2 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +20 **Ref** +26 **Will** +23 **HP** 240 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** [bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), [death effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=2331), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Weaknesses** slashing 10 **Bound Limbs** A torn quartet ordinarily has four severed limbs tethered to a central point by near-incorporeal ropes. A limb is essentially cut away from the central point and rendered nonfunctional each time the torn quartet loses 60 Hit Points (so at 180 Hit Points, the torn quartet has three functional limbs, at 120 Hit Points, it has two functional limbs, and so on. Each functioning limb can [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) separate creatures within reach, or multiple functioning limbs can Grapple the same creature) for each additional limb used to Grapple a creature, the [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) DC increases by 2.
**Replacement Parts** A torn quartet can spend 1 minute tearing apart the corpse of a humanoid creature that was killed within the last hour to regain 60 Hit Points and restore one of its nonfunctioning limbs. A torn quartet can't have more than four limbs.
**Split Reactions** A torn quartet has a number of reactions per round equal to its number of still-functioning limbs, which it can use only to make Reactive Strikes. It can't use more than 1 reaction on the same triggering action, even if a creature leaves several squares within its reach, and the torn quartet must use a different limb for each Reactive Strike it makes. Whenever one of the torn quartet's limbs is rendered nonfunctional, the torn quartet loses one of its reactions.
**Reactive Strike** See Split Reactions. --- **Speed** 10 feet, fly 30 feet **Melee** limb +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d8+13 bludgeoning plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Flurry of Limbs** The torn quartet makes a number of limb Strikes up to its number of functioning limbs, each against a different target. These attacks count toward the torn quartet's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the torn quartet makes all its attacks. **Tear Asunder** **Requirements** The torn quartet has a creature [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by at least two limbs; **Effect** The creature takes 5d6 slashing damage for each limb currently grabbing or restraining it (maximum 15d6), with a DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the creature also loses a random body part, and one of the torn quartet's limbs is now no longer grabbing or restraining it.

features.Bloodthirsty Plants:
([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** An enemy in the tree singer's Verdant Aria aura (see below) attacks one of the tree singer's allies; **Effect** Vines and branches to lash out at the attacker, dealing 3d6 piercing damage.
**Plant Empathy** The tree singer can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) skill with [plants](/Traits.aspx?ID=668) and [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=614).

features.Verdant Aria: <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [Plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508)) The tree singer raises their voice in a haunting melody, creating an aura in a 30-foot emanation. Plants in the aura seem to come to life, swaying and rustling in response to the music. The tree singer's allies in the aura gain a +2 status bonus to AC and saving throws as the foliage around them shields and defends them from harm. The aura lasts until the end of the tree singer's next turn but can be Sustained. It can be Sustained even if the tree singer is [polymorphed](/Traits.aspx?ID=670). The effect ends early if the tree singer stops singing.

description: Singers can speak the words of creation in song, a forgotten art from the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=35). Their melodies turn grass into blades and make trees stir. Through their music, plants rise to defend and seek vengeance for nature. Taught by woodland spirits or [fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119) agents of the First World, they master the magic of primal song.

Twins of rowan are among the most powerful elementals on the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25), specially crafted to patrol a wide range of wilderness and maintain the plane's carefully constructed order. Despite having two heads and torsos, each twins of rowan is a singular creature; like all wood elementals, their true consciousness is not in their heads but in the roots, and their true body is the trunk of the tree, not the extended limbs. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Recall Knowledge - Plant](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 31 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 29 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 26 [Twins of Rowan](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2680) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 211 2.0 **Perception** +26; [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 30 feet **Languages** [Arboreal](/Languages.aspx?ID=26), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +24, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +26, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +21 **Str** +5 **Dex** +4 **Con** +8 **Int** +2 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +4 **Shielded Eyes** A twins of rowan's protective mask
shields them from [blinding](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) and [dazzling](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) effects. --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +17 **Will** +27 **HP** 273 **Immunities** bleed, [blindness](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1), [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Weaknesses** [axes](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=1) 15, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 15 **Beacon of the Rowan Guard** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508)) 40 feet. The lantern carried by the twins of rowan contains pure elemental life energy that resonates with and empowers all wood elementals. While within the emanation, a creature with the [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) trait and either the [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) trait or [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait gains [fast healing 10](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=15) and a +2 circumstance bonus to all attack and damage rolls. The aura can be [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) with a DC 30 check to [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78); doing so deactivates the aura for 1d6 rounds. --- **Speed** 35 feet, climb 25 feet **Melee** rapier +26 ([deadly d8](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [Disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 4d8+5 piercing **Melee** fist +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+5 bludgeoning **Ranged** stump +26 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 2d10+15 bludgeoning **Follow-Up Combo** The twins of rowan makes a rapier Strike, followed by two fist Strikes, all against the same target. These attacks all count toward the twins' multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after the twins make their attacks. **Lifespring Burst** ([Plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), [Primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134), [Vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) Once per day, the twins of rowan can strike the ground with their sword, releasing a 30-foot burst of life energy centered on the twins that deals 14d6 vitality damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save); the twins of rowan is immune. The area affected by this burst then becomes [greater difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) as vibrant new plant life ruptures through it. **Throw Stump** As [Throw Rock](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=38) but can also be used to throw stumps and logs.

The most powerful zuhras draw followers and elemental metal with overwhelming force of personality and literal magnetism. When called upon to conduct _wish_ rituals, they use their long isolation from the other planes as an excuse to misinterpret requests outlandishly, claiming linguistic differences. **[Recall Knowledge - Elemental](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Zuhra Shuyookh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2656) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 161 2.0 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +27, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +24, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +26, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +26, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +24, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +28, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +22 **Str** +5 **Dex** +6 **Con** +8 **Int** +5 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +7 **Items** _+2 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [spiked chain](/Weapons.aspx?ID=60)_ --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +29 **Ref** +23 **Will** +21 **HP** 212 **Resistances** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) 10 **Conductive Redirection** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56)) **Trigger** The zuhra is hit by an attack, spell, or effect that deals electricity damage; **Effect** The zuhra conducts the electricity through their body, taking damage as normal, and redirecting a bolt at one target within 30 feet that they can see. The zuhra makes a ranged attack roll with a +27 modifier against the target's AC. On a hit or critical hit, the target takes electricity damage equal to the full damage of the triggering effect.
**Magnetic Field** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505)) 10 feet. All squares in the aura are [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for creatures wearing metal armor or made of metal. Strikes with metallic weapons made by or against creatures in this aura take a –2 status penalty to the attack roll. Zuhras ignore these effects. --- **Speed** 30 feet, fly 35 feet **Melee** _spiked chain_ +27 ([Disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=175), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192), [Trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196)), **Damage** 2d8+11 slashing plus 1d12 electricity **Melee** hand blade +25 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d4+11 slashing plus 4d4 [persistent bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 32, attack +24 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) - **5th** [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) (×2), [Magnetic Acceleration](/Spells.aspx?ID=943) (at will), [Magnetic Attraction](/Spells.aspx?ID=944) (at will) - **6th** [Mercurial Stride](/Spells.aspx?ID=1374), [Wall of Metal](/Spells.aspx?ID=1379) - **7th** [Clad in Metal](/Spells.aspx?ID=1366) (can choose uncommon and rare metals), [Enthrall](/Spells.aspx?ID=104), [Plane Shift](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) (at will; to [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=8), Elemental Planes, or the [Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) only), [Weapon Storm](/Spells.aspx?ID=373) - **Constant (5th)** [Tongues](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) **[Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8)** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [Polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) The zuhra transforms into a Small or Medium metal elemental or animal. This doesn't affect the zuhra's statistics, but it could change the damage type of their Strikes. **Magnetic Reposition** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The shuyookh targets any number of creatures affected by their magnetic field, and [moves](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) each target 10 feet in a direction the zuhra chooses. Each target can resist being moved if it succeeds at a DC 32 Fortitude save. **Magnetic Storm** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11)) **Requirements** The shuyookh's magnetic field is active; **Effect** The shuyookh electromagnetically flings razor-sharp metal scraps. Each creature in a 30-foot emanation takes 8d6 slashing damage and 3d12 electricity damage, with a DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. The shuyookh's magnetic field is deactivated for 1d4 rounds. **Mercurial Wish** ([Downtime](/Traits.aspx?ID=49)) **Frequency** three times per year; **Effect** The shuyookh conducts a _wish_ ritual for the benefit of a mortal, requiring no cost or secondary casters. The shuyookh's result is a success if they succeed at a DC 5 flat check or a failure if not. The shuyookh attempts to fulfill the wish in a way that creates an unstable or impermanent benefit.

The three major celestial planes—[Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=41), [Nirvana](/Planes.aspx?ID=44), and [Elysium](/Planes.aspx?ID=40)—each have their own respective dragons. Fortune dragons have the innate ability to draw upon the raw magical energies that surround them. They constantly use these magical energies to empower their magical abilities and even their bodies, as the energy can heal wounds. A fortune dragon has a typical build for an arcane dragon, but their bodies sport a striking feature: their treasure. The dragon's nature of drawing upon magic causes coins, gems, and, most notably, magical items to cling to their body like iron drawn to magnets. A dragon constantly pulls magical energies from the items attached to their body and makes use of these energies to cast spells. The magical energies that flow through a fortune dragon constantly flow through the dragon's items as well, and in many cases, the items melt from the heat produced in this process. Fortune dragons are seekers of novel experiences. This desire for originality leads fortune dragons to approach visitors of other ancestries with curiosity, though this initial interest quickly wanes if a visitor lacks exciting qualities. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 32 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 30 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 [Adult Fortune Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2945) **Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 118 1.1 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3) **Skills** [Accounting Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +28, [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +27, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +28, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +27, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +28, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +24, [Mercantile Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +28, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) +27 **Str** +7 **Dex** +7 **Con** +6 **Int** +8 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +4 --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +27 **Will** +24 +2 status to all saves vs. [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) **HP** 230 **Immunities** [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Aura of Disruption** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542)) 120 feet. The dragon radiates disruptive energies that allow them to feed on magic. **Capture Spell** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Trigger** The dragon succeeds or critically succeeds on a saving throw against a spell; **Effect** The dragon attempts to capture a portion of the spell's magic to feed themself. The dragon's body is then no longer covered in riches. **Treasure Dive** **Requirements** The dragon's body isn't covered in riches and the dragon is adjacent to their hoard; **Effect** The dragon Strides or [Burrows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) through their hoard using their land Speed. The brutish and gluttonous augnagar live to feast—preferably on rotten flesh and, when possible, demon flesh. But to them, the greatest delicacy is the flesh of other augnagars. Augnagars have swollen, spiderlike legs with leathery membranes like a bat's wings, and three tails ending in hooked stings perfect for slicing flesh. An augnagar that gorges sufficiently, especially on other augnagars, can grow so massive it can't even move, thrashing and festering where it lies. It eventually flies into a frenzy of self-cannibalism as it rips apart its own flesh to feast on. description:
The brutish and gluttonous augnagar live to feast—preferably on rotten flesh and, when possible, demon flesh. But to them, the greatest delicacy is the flesh of other augnagars. Augnagars have swollen, spiderlike legs with leathery membranes like a bat's wings, and three tails ending in hooked stings perfect for slicing flesh.

 An augnagar that gorges sufficiently, especially on other augnagars, can grow so massive it can't even move, thrashing and festering where it lies. It eventually flies into a frenzy of self-cannibalism as it rips apart its own flesh to feast on. From the ruinous remains emerges a [thulgant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=777)—a smaller but more powerful qlippoth.

<title level="1" pfs="Standard">[Brass Bastion](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2631)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Brass bastions are formidable sentinels crafted from elemental fire and extraplanar brass. While they can be shaped into many forms, most depict muscular warriors with curving horns and stern or taunting expressions. Within each brass shell is a raging inferno—the source of its ceaseless heat. Though ifrits originally created brass bastions to act as servants and guards, the knowledge of how to craft them has spread throughout the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6). They can even be found on the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=5) thanks to interplanar trade. In Medina Mudii'a, brass bastions walk the streets, tend shops, and stand guard. Bespoke brass bastions are passed down as family heirlooms or gifted to business partners and allies. Scions of the wealthiest ifrit lineages never travel without a train of brass bastions clad in family livery. Destroying a rival ifrit's brass bastion is a quick way to erode their political status, though anyone caught performing such sabotage faces swift retribution.

 Most brass bastions prominently display the sigil of their owner or maker, though magical methods can also determine who crafted a specific construct. Brass bastions forged by favored artisans are a status symbol in many ifrit communities. Ifrits consider a brass bastion crafted by a non-ifrit to be inherently inferior, barely worth the cost of its materials. Brass bastions obey magical programming imprinted at the time of their creation or follow commands from their owners. Most can't speak, but a few have magical voices and can parrot simple phrases, recite poetry, or tell bedtime stories at the crafter's fancy.

Bul-gaes are manifestations of the eclipsed sun and moon. They look like large canines, though their coloration and features change as they exercise their powers over heat and cold. Depending on whether they've most recently unleashed their lunar or solar powers, bul-gaes resemble either a crimson hound wreathed in flames or a cerulean, frostbitten fox, respectively. Legends say that the first bul-gae attempted to steal the sun from the sky. As they bit down on the burning sphere, though, the bul-gae was badly burned. Having failed, they then tried to retrieve the moon, but when they touched the moon, the bul-gae froze solid and fell to the ground. The descendants of that bul-gae forever hone their powers of flame and ice so that they might one day succeed where their ancestor failed. Tales say that bul-gaes serve as faithful companions to the ancient, shadowy master of the first bul-gae. The magma remains until the start of the linnorm's next turn. If the linnorm was on the ground, the magma remains as a burning line on the ground directly under the line of the Magma Breath; if the linnorm was airborne, the magma rains down in a sheet 60 feet high. Any creature that moves across or through the magma takes 6d6 fire damage (DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). <title level="1" pfs="">[Crowded Veil](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3787)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Only one crowded veil exists, but it does so as separate entities in many different bodies. As each “individual” member shares a core extraplanar essence with the others, communication between them moves without regard to planar boundaries or the limitations of distance, allowing for swift transmission of information throughout Tanglebriar and beyond.

<column gap="tiny">
**[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 37

**[Recall Knowledge - Fungus](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**
([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 37

**[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35

**[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32
</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>

<title level="2" right="Creature 14">[Crowded Veil](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3787)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Fiend" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=600" />
<trait label="Fungus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=614" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 80

**Perception** +28; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 120 feet

**Languages**
[Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119); (cannot speak); spore telepathy

**Skills**
[Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +26, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +28, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +25

<row gap="medium">
**Str** +6

**Dex** +5

**Con** +5

**Int** +5

**Wis** +8

**Cha** +4
</row>

**Spore Telepathy** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 60 feet. A crowded veil communicates telepathically via spores. It can communicate telepathically with any creatures who are within its aura.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 33 

**Fort** +25 

**Ref** +22 

**Will** +28 

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**HP** 300
(one mind)

</row>

**Immunities**
[blind](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95)

**Resistances**
[mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 15

**Weaknesses**
[fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 15, [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 15, slashing 15

**One Mind** A crowded veil is an individual creature that shares one mind with all other crowded veils. What one crowded veil experiences, all experience. If a crowded veil gains any conditions, all other crowded veils know this; they also know the direction to every other crowded veil and the distances between them. A crowded veil can communicate instantly and telepathically with any other crowded veil on the same planet. To crowded veils located on other planets, messages can take up to an hour or more to transmit. A message to a crowded veil on another plane takes 24 hours to transmit. A crowded veil is immune to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects that target only a specific number of creatures. If a mental effect targets all creatures in an area, only the crowded veils in that area are affected, although all other crowded veils sense all damage or conditions endured by those crowded veils.

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 20 feet; fly 30 feet

**Melee**
<actions string="Single Action" />
tentacle +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170)),
**Damage** 3d8+14 bludgeoning

**Ranged**
<actions string="Single Action" />
spore pod +28 ([Brutal](/Traits.aspx?ID=249), [Propulsive](/Traits.aspx?ID=191), [range 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)),
**Damage** 3d6+11 bludgeoning plus crowded veil spores

**Primal Innate Spells** DC 31
- **Constant (7th)**
[Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727)

**Crowded Veil Spores**  ([Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 34; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) (1 round); **Stage 2** 4d8 poison damage and stupefied 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 4d8 poison damage and stupefied 3 (1 round); **Stage 4** 4d8 poison damage and [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) (1 round)

**Spore Trail** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([Manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) A crowded veil shudders, releasing toxic spores. Until the end of their turn, when the clouded veil moves, all spaces they leave are filled with spores. These spore trails persist until the start of the clouded veil's next turn, and can be dispersed immediately by wind in the area. The first time in a round when a creature enters this spore trail, that creature is exposed to crowded veil spores.

</column>

<aside>
